…SCP-682 burst into my office, before being destroyed by an MTF rocket launcher. It took a moment for my brain to register that the Dragon was really dead. 682, the unkillable, was dead! However, I'd been splattered with the stuff. They tossed me in quarantine. When they conducted their tests, they discovered I had acquired the shapeshifting powers by absorbing some of its tissue, and I was secreting the fluid myself!

I didn't know I could cringe that hard. Turns out I can.
They should have offered the guy to roll around in whatever 173 secretes. Just in case it works out.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
How about a loop paradox?

The Foundation wonder-tech slowly leeches out to the general scientific community and public at large; either through leaks or deliberate well-intentioned efforts to boost progress. Eventually, as the present catches up to the searched dates, there comes a point where a journal or paper only gets published because of the Foundations prompting. The research would not have happened if the Foundation hadn't pulled the data from the future. But the data was only there to be pulled because the Foundation would have had already done so (time travel needs it's own conjugation). Cause without effect, in an endless logic loop. The cosmos can't handle the strain, all the laws of continuity break down. Temporal chaos, with anachronisms and discontinuities everywhere; T-Rex in Times Square, the Kittyhawk Flyer has a mid-air collision with the Enola Gay, dogs and cats living together, mass hysteria! The haggard, pitiful remnants of the human race, willing to sarifice their very existence to thwart the madness that has overtaken reality; exploit a particularly extreme rift in the continum to reach back to a pivotal moment. They only have a few seconds of window back to that oh so clever junior researcher, and only a few grams of matter could ever fit through this particular gap in time. But it's enough, and the choosen gunman had excellent aim.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Well, here's my contribution:

Late one night, the former researcher-turned-head researcher was browsing files 50 years into the future when he noticed something unusual. The last Scientific American .zip file had come with an economic spreadsheet. He opened them on a whim, and he noticed that as the years went by, the income and total profit of the magazine dropped sharply, almost to the point where one year’s worth of issues could be funded by pocket money of a 15 year-old. Wanting to know more, he downloaded a .zip file 51 years into the future, and all his horrible suspicions were confirmed: the magazine’s cover was emblazoned with grainy, low-res photos of “cryptids”, and the side captions screamed, “UNCOFIRMED WITNESS REPORTS! LAKE SUPERIOR MONSTER! FIVE DEAD!” He then turned to the first page, and read in small text.
“This magazine brought to you by the Unusual Incidents Unit.”
The researcher rushed to the phone to talk to the O5s as soon as possible, but it was too late. The brand-new containment cells designed of “Hypernium, the Indestructible Metal” to house Keter-class SCPs all collapsed. The site’s lighting, powered by “Orgonean energy” and “Minovsky particles “failed, and SCP-173 went on a massacre. The “grey-hole” technology that could supposedly “teleport” personnel at no risk were indirectly responsible for the deaths of staff, as they predictably also didn’t work.
The Serpent’s Hand saw our newfound weakness, and took the opportunity to strike. Most of us died in the first wave, and the rest 20 or so of us managed to find an empty concrete bunker under the site. I broadcast this message in the hopes that some will hear us. It’s been two months. In this three-way war between the Foundation, the Serpent’s Hand, and the Keters, I don’t think the human race can survive.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
How about this:

79's only prgrammed goal is self-improvement. All 732 wants is to write itself in as the hero in an epic story. So that's exactly what "The Penitent" did. The combined entity wrote itself in as the hero in the best possible story, human history. The problem is that none of it is real. The breakthroughs, the peace, the entire golden age is just an illusion caused by the fictionalized reports. Every computerized record and piece of data (which is pretty much all data these days) says that there are no disasters and nothing to worry about because The Penitent has fixed everything. So nobody works to put out the wildfires or quarantine the plauge or re-contain the SCP-XXXX breach. The only people who know something is wrong are the people who actually witness something themselves, and by the time that is enough people to convince the rest of the world it's too late and the damage is too extensive to be fixed.

If only I had a decent utopia idea, I'd write it in.

item.title: Re: Breach in Tone?
item.content:encoded: That's intentional. How this works is that you take the last person's happy ending and show how using that particular SCP actually ended up destroying the world or otherwise being a bad thing. Then you right a new happy ending using a different SCP. And someone else destroys the world using it, etc.
